newsitem.title: USA: St. Louis Mayor announces new health clinic board.
newsitem.headline: St. Louis Mayor announces new health clinic board.

text.p: St. Louis Mayor Clarence Harmon announced Thursday the formation of a new health care corporation to operate four city clinics for the indigent after a regional hospital now running them closes in a few months.

Under the agreement, St. Louis Regional Medical Center, commonly known as Regional Hospital, will operate the clinics for up to 90 days in a transition period before a tax-exempt not-for-profit corporation called Newco takes control of the network, Harmon said.
St. Louis will provide $1 million in fiscal 1998 for capital improvements at the clinics using proceeds from a refinancing of outstanding stadium bonds, Harmon said.
The city will also guarantee a $5 million interest-free loan for new clinic equipment for the clinics, which Newco will run for up to five years, Harmon said.
During the life of Newco's contract with St. Louis, the city will also provide approximately $1.9 million of general relief funding, Harmon added.
The Newco board will include three mayoral appointees, one St. Louis County member, a Missouri representative, six private health care systems members and two community representatives.
"I am hopeful that the regional board will now do its part in placing the health care needs of this community above all other considerations," Harmon said.

Regional Hospital had been licensed for 304 beds when it opened, but had been using about 35 beds in recent months, Harmon said. Only about one-third of those patients lacked health care or Medicaid coverage, he added.
Participating hospitals have committed to accepting all uninsured patients referred by the clinics, Harmon said, adding that he expects most clinic employees to remain with the facilities.
